entities.summary: Gasparo Cairano, also known as Gasparo da Cairano, de Cayrano, da Milano, Coirano, and other variations, was an Italian Renaissance sculptor of unknown birth and death in 1517. He was born in Milan, Italy, during the Renaissance period, a time marked by great artistic innovation and cultural upheaval. Cairano worked primarily in Milan, and his works are characterized by their technical skill and emotional depth, often exploring themes of love, sacrifice, and redemption. His sculptures can be found in various churches and cathedrals throughout Italy, including the Milanese Duomo. Cairano's legacy can be seen in the works of later Italian Renaissance sculptors, who built upon his techniques and innovations. He played a significant role in the development of Renaissance sculpture, helping to establish Milan as a major artistic center. Cairano's works are now highly regarded for their beauty, emotion, and historical significance. The artist's use of marble and other materials allowed him to create highly detailed and realistic sculptures, often depicting scenes from mythology and the Bible.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cairano's sculptures had a lasting impact on the development of Renaissance art, influencing later artists such as Michelangelo and Donatello. His works helped establish Milan as a major artistic center, attracting artists and patrons from across Italy.
